Looping in a quick workaround and a couple of tips - we hit this frequently across APAC/EU customers, especially around DST transitions.

Camila / Alex - short checklist:
- Calendly: ensure "Show invitee their timezone" is enabled in Account > Event Type > When. If the invitee's browser has a different locale it can still force a mismatch; the dropdown near the top-right lets the invitee override it.
- Chili Piper: for some flows you can append a query param to force the timezone, e.g. "?tz=Asia/Singapore" or use "force_timezone=true" in the booking URL. Our SRE team sometimes seeds the flow with the invitee timezone to avoid confusion.
- Manual ICS workaround: create the calendar event in the target timezone (e.g., Asia/Singapore), export as .ics and send as an attachment from your Redwood calendar. That ensures the recipient's calendar client interprets the time correctly.
- DST gotcha: EU switches to DST on Sun Mar 29 this year - if you're booking across that boundary, double-check the timezone offsets for dates before/after the switch.

Alex - I can create the invite in SGT for Wed Mar 25 16:00 SGT and send the .ics from the Redwood org calendar (that method has worked reliably). Camila, if you want I'll create it and send from marissa@redwood.com so it has the org calendar metadata.
